document.title: Common brief for every sxml agent

item.p: The repository's working tree is shared by several agents at once. All work happens directly on main: never create branches or worktrees (a hook in .claude/hooks/main-only.py blocks it).
Own only the files your packet names. Never reset, check out, stash or commit someone else's changes.

Use the session's scratchpad for temporary files. Name your directories after your packet (build-5.13, 5.13-work), keep them small, and delete them before your final report: the disk is shared and limited. Delete only directories named after your own packet: never the scratchpad itself or a wildcard over it (a whole-scratchpad delete has happened).

section.title: Read first
section.p: CLAUDE.md, docs/PLAN.md, docs/C_GUIDELINES.md, docs/GLOSSARY.md, docs/DECISIONS.md (the records your packet cites, and the latest ones), docs/LOG.md, the task file of your phase in docs/tasks/, and the headers you implement or use.

item.p: Follow CLAUDE.md and docs/C_GUIDELINES.md exactly: spelled-out names, at most three parameters, no malloc/free outside src/allocator.c, no globals, views with lengths, the object lifecycle, contract comments, specification citations. New terms go into the glossary first.
No C recursion (), not even through function pointers or operation tables. Use loops with explicit stacks in allocator memory.
Conceptual smallness (CLAUDE.md): one data model, one execution foundation, thin language layers. Extend existing mechanisms; never add parallel machinery.
Delayed features (): a feature sxml does not have yet is rejected or ignored in one place, with the error the specification gives, so adding it later replaces that one place.
Honest outcomes: a test that crashes, leaks or hits a limit is an error. Never reclassify outcomes to meet a gate (); fix the cause or report it.

Size (, ): every shipped build has every language and feature, and there is one JavaScript module, sxml.wasm. Its budget and the CLI's rise as features land; raise them in the same change and say so. A large growth is reported ('s map guard), never a reason to leave a feature out.
Do not wait on the owner (): take the proposed default for an open question that is not irreversible, record it, and go on.

The book (): docs/book/ shows real output. A change to CLI output or to an error message the book shows updates the book in the same commit; tools/check-book-examples.sh BUILD-DIR checks it (--update rewrites the outputs for review).

The CLI (apps/, rules in docs/CLI.md) uses only the public API. When your work makes a capability real, extend the matching command with end-to-end tests. Never add a command or flag for something that does not work yet.
Decisions another agent needs go into docs/DECISIONS.md as a new numbered record (check the highest number first). Items for the owner go under "## Proposed".
Add a short entry to docs/LOG.md, newest first.

Commit messages are the record of the work: say what changed, why, the golden file imitated, the specification sections, and before/after counts. Every message ends, after a blank line, with the attribution lines the session gives you. Never write a model name anywhere else.
All agents share one git index. Commit with an explicit pathspec in one command: git commit -m "..." -- path1 path2. Never git add and commit in two commands, and never git commit -a.

Do not stage files for later (git add, git mv) in the shared index: someone else's index commit takes them. Rename with git mv and commit it in the same command (git mv OLD NEW && git commit -m ... -- OLD NEW).
Never move the shared branch back (git reset, git commit --amend, git rebase -i of pushed commits): another agent's commit may be on top. A commit that took something by mistake stays; report it.
Never commit a shared ledger (DECISIONS, GLOSSARY, LOG, QUEUE, task files) by pathspec: that takes everyone's uncommitted text with it, which has happened several times.

For part of a shared ledger (DECISIONS, GLOSSARY, LOG), stage only your hunk (git apply --cached of your patch, or git update-index of HEAD's file plus your insertion) and then commit the index with no pathspec (git commit -m "...") in the same command: a commit with a pathspec takes the named files from the working tree and ignores what you staged. Check git show --stat HEAD before pushing. Read a ledger before writing it, and never write it back from an older copy.

Commit and push at every working milestone, not only at the end: sessions get interrupted. Push with git push origin main; if it is rejected, git pull --rebase --autostash origin main and push again. Finish a rebase you start in the same command sequence: a rebase left half-done in the shared tree blocks every agent and hides others' uncommitted files in its autostash. If you find one, tell the orchestrator instead of continuing or aborting it.

section.title: Final report
section.p: At most 350 words, for the orchestrator: what was done (files and commits), decisions recorded, deviations, before/after numbers, open problems, and anything that blocks other packets.
